note: Epiphany Aquarium split from EpiphanyAgent so the UI can evolve under its own pseudo-Epiphany state, memory, and taste doctrine. Backend harness scripts still live in EpiphanyAgent; the aquarium repo owns interaction, WebGL, audio, and visual smoke.

lesson: The aquarium behavior contract is now mapped in notes/aquarium-behavior-map.md: snapshot bridge -> React projection -> DOM agents -> renderer/fluid/audio -> Tauri actions. The main design debt is preserving the old operator console as one gated panel instead of splitting it into agent-owned organs.

The selected-agent focus surface no longer mounts the generic operator console. App.tsx now renders agent-owned habitats: Self intent/command, Imagination planning, Eyes evidence/artifacts, Body graph/modeling, Hands workspace/implementation, Soul findings/risk, and Life continuity/memory. Future work should deepen distinct silhouettes instead of re-centralizing the panel cluster.

The aquarium interaction hierarchy should be grounded in EpiphanyAgent API seam families, not inherited UI tabs. Branch nodes are cute icons over read/write/proposal/runtime families; leaf nodes expose specific seams such as CRRC, graphQuery, planning drafts, roleResult, reorientVerdict, or continueImplementation.

Face is now a first-class aquarium creature, not only a future Discord adapter. Its local habitat can read heartbeat status, run a heartbeat slot, and open a Discord-independent bubble artifact via EpiphanyAgent's GUI action bridge.

Thought bubbles and heartbeat belong to every aquarium creature. The backend heartbeat remains a shared pulse, but each habitat now exposes Heartbeat -> Status/Pulse locally; Face keeps Bubble as the public mouth for shared heartbeat output.

Agent motion should expose its orbit model directly: thin dashed gradient guides in the crisp canvas, spring tethering to orbit slots, pointer attraction as a local perturbation, and touch/heartbeat chirps as damped plucked-string oscillations across motion and audio.

Shared heartbeat is universal creature life, not just the latest awakened role. All agents should show heartbeat-driven pluck energy; the latest selected heartbeat role gets the stronger local oscillation and notification burst.

Pointer attraction should be field-shaped, not a single strong tug. At long range most creatures attract weakly, Self repels weakly, and at short range all creatures attract strongly so the cursor can deliberately pull an object out of orbit.

The pointer field should feel like invitation, not intrusion. Long-range repulsion belongs only to Soul, and only weakly; other creatures should attract gently at range and all creatures should attract strongly only at close range.

Aquarium gravity should follow Aetheria's zone contract: objects hover at heightfield height plus offset, gravity wells render as cups beneath them, and force comes from the heightfield normal scaled by horizontal slope squared so both far edges and well centers are gentle.

Aetheria's real compute stardust translates to the aquarium as optional WebGPU: compute updates particle storage buffers, render draws instanced quads, and the compatible WebGL2 path remains the surface/ink fallback. Until fluid moves to WebGPU, mirror visible flow sources rather than pretending WebGPU can sample WebGL velocity textures directly.

The aquarium should read as a camera above a grid, not a flat HUD. Keep agent simulation in grid coordinates, project DOM and surface rendering through a tilted overhead camera, and unproject cursor screen input back to the grid before using it as force or a landing marker.

Aquarium now has a swarm registry seam: Tauri loads `.epiphany-aquarium/swarm.json`, scopes status/actions/artifacts to the selected member, and can register AetheriaLore as a workspace Epiphany instance using the shared EpiphanyAgent harness with repo-local `.epiphany` state.

Current Aetheria gravity rendering is a render-target pipeline, not a per-vertex source enumeration. Gravity wells and wave brushes should splat as additive top-down quads into a grid-aligned gravity texture; the visible mesh then samples the accumulated field. Aquarium's Three layer now mirrors that model and maps low agent chirp-bank partials into radial speaker-like grid vibrations.

Three scene interaction must use one shared XY plane: render-target gravity splats, visible grid displacement, projected cursor, camera pan/orbit, and agent deltas all measure against XY with Z as height. Middle drag orbits, wheel zooms exponentially, and right drag/WASD pan the camera target.

Swarm Aquarium now treats API contracts as user-story contracts: selected members may only operate inside their registered workspace, codex-home overrides are ignored in favor of registry authority, and cross-agent blockers move through visible coordinator messages instead of cross-workspace rummaging. Humans inspect internals richly but talk to Face; sub-agents communicate through typed coordinator lanes.

The Three camera must be a true orbital camera over the aquarium grid: a target point on XY, polar yaw/pitch/distance converted to Cartesian position, and camera.up fixed to +Z before lookAt. Pan vectors should come from the projected view direction so WASD/right drag match what the user sees.

For pointer-driven camera panning, sample consecutive mouse ray intersections on the shared XY plane and move the camera target by previous-hit minus next-hit. Projected deltas cancel out perspective/orbit basis issues better than hand-maintained pan vectors.

After the Three grid becomes the visual authority, DOM creature icons, thought bubbles, option halos, focus surfaces, stardust attractors, and pointer-to-grid input must consume the same Three camera projection/unprojection. Old percent-space faux perspective is only a fallback.

Aetheria's Stardust.compute does not integrate millions of independent particle histories. It derives particles from moving grid cells, uses hashed cell coordinates so paired particles share stable lifetime phase, samples field/tint, and offsets by flow(position) * lifetime * period for pseudo-continuous flow with minimal stored state.

Aquarium stardust can run at one million particles by keeping the Aetheria moving-cell derivation model and removing CPU seed uploads. The compute pass owns every particle before draw, so startup should allocate the storage buffer without pushing a huge initialized array across the bus.

Dense stardust should be treated as HDR light, not ordinary alpha decoration: tiny faint motes accumulate into an rgba16float target and pass through ACES tonemapping. The current overlay does this locally; the long-term renderer should share one HDR post chain across stardust, grid, fluid, and creature glow.

Invisible radial option buttons can still intercept creature clicks when children have pointer-events:auto. Keep option buttons pointer-inert until the halo is open/hot, and keep disabled option buttons pointer-inert so the creature body remains clickable.

Crisp aquarium UI can stay DOM/SVG while becoming diegetic: mount the SVG/DOM surface as a camera-facing billboard in world space near a creature, then ray-project the cursor onto the billboard plane and translate the local hit into DOM control coordinates.

Visual smoke creature-tree clicks must wait for the next branch node after a synthetic click. Heavy GPU overlays can delay React paint enough that immediate query-after-dispatch fails even when real interaction works.

A million-particle HDR stardust pass should not submit on every animation frame by default. Capping its cadence around 30fps preserves main-thread/UI responsiveness while keeping the dense field alive.

Visual smoke should not use the full million-particle stardust load in headless browsers. Use a smoke query flag to keep the shader/compositor path active at lower particle count, and verify the normal million-particle path with a separate targeted probe.

Broad visual smoke should not test cursor-driven aquarium interaction once UI surfaces are projected through 3D/billboard math. Keep smoke to rendering/layout presence; write targeted raycast-aware probes for creature-tree and billboard hit testing.

Diegetic DOM panels should not share the creature body projection point. Emit separate Three-projected anchors for body, option halo, thought bubble, and focus surface, then render DOM/SVG as camera-facing billboard slabs with local pointer coordinates for crisp interaction.

Visible non-DOM aquarium elements must share the Three/HDR compositor. Separate screen-space particle/crisp/smoke canvases can remain as compatibility mounts, but making them visible splits projection, tone mapping, and user trust.
The 3D object is the creature body; the centered DOM caption is the ID tag and interaction-graph root. Keep text in DOM, hide duplicate glyph-body icons, and spawn radial controls around the caption.
When the pointer is inside a creature billboard, hold that creature's orbit integration. A menu that drifts under the cursor reads as broken even if the projection math is technically alive.

DOM labels and billboards must project from the actual Three body transform after easing, not from the next grid target. Otherwise the object can visibly lag its caption or caption lag its object depending on which path has smoothing.

Do not add a second smoothing layer in Three for agent body positions. Fluid projection already integrates motion; Three-side lerp makes DOM labels and 3D bodies drift out of phase, most visibly on Self.

Self must not be a special physics class. Multiple Epiphanies require role-symmetric spring bodies: orbit slots, mouse attachment, hover hold, pluck impulse, and future inter-Epiphany approach are all forces in one accumulator.
Camera zoom should change the visible grid cell scale and information level. Project labels belong as world-space DOM billboards that fade in at far zoom, not as always-on screen-space UI.

The cursor spring should be implicit: render the cursor as a gravity well and compute the pull as that field's gradient, keeping pointer interaction in the same force language as agents and future Epiphany-to-Epiphany attraction.
Grid zoom must resize the actual rendered grid geometry, not only the procedural cell spacing. Keep gravity wells in fixed world coordinates while expanding the field mesh with camera distance.
Zoomed-out workspace labels should replace sub-agent captions, not stack with them. Harness/workspace labels are interaction roots with their own radial petals.

The Self/coordinator cohesion field should be visible as a large shared swarm gravity divot, and the force holding agents in orbit should be computed from gravity gradients rather than hidden linear springs.

When only one agent swarm is rendered, show only that active harness menu. Anchor the harness menu at the centroid of the rendered sub-agent bodies, not at an invented swarm-member ring or above the centroid.

Grid waves driven by chirp banks need spectral shaping: low bands should have wide slow breathing waves around 0.5-1 Hz, while high bands need rolled-off amplitude, smaller radii, and sub-unit world wavelengths so treble reads as shimmer instead of broad gravity heave.

Stardust should be parented to the grid transform and use particle spawn/position offsets, not alpha, to express density around the displaced gravity surface. Above-grid offsets can use a broader exponential distribution; below-grid offsets need a sharper exponential falloff.

Camera exploration needs one moving gravity-field origin shared by the visible grid mesh, deferred gravity orthographic camera, grid shader UVs, and parented stardust sampling. Scaling the grid without moving the field origin leaves the user panning away from the floor.

Aetheria-style stardust should treat buffer particles as temporary workers for world-space cells. Derive jitter, height, lifetime, size, and color from hashed world cell coordinates around the moving camera/grid origin, then fade at the field edge so a different buffer slot can take over the same star without visible discontinuity.

For Aquarium GPU work, think like a compute specialist: design explicit passes and ownership, minimize CPU readback, use workgroup-local memory and barriers for cooperative tile reuse, keep global/storage access coherent, splat sparse sources into deferred fields, and derive identity from stable domains when stored particle identity is unnecessary.

GigaVoxels-style rendering treats rays as demand signals: sparse tree metadata plus dense brick pools represent fields larger than GPU memory, traversal records visible/missing LOD needs, coarser resident data is used as fallback, and timestamps/LRU stream only the working set required by current view and temporal coherence.

Wroński-style volumetric fog is a froxel field pipeline: inject density, light, shadows, anisotropy, noise, and local fog volumes into a camera-aligned 3D texture; run a depth-wise Beer-Lambert scattering/transmittance scan; then composite by sampling the accumulated volume with screen UV and scene depth. Production stability depends on low-pass shadow/filter choices, jitter/temporal filtering, explicit range/resolution tradeoffs, and honest approximations for special lights.

The Dreams talk transcript adds constraints and implementation lessons missing from slide text alone: no imported textures/models/meshes, PS4/controller-native authoring, SDF edit lists being less intimidating than topology, chained compute-shader pipelines becoming unmaintainable, atomic point splatting, TAA as a stochastic resolver, imperfect shadow maps, noisy AO/voxel occlusion, and point-jitter DOF succeeding where naive point-jitter motion blur fails because motion blur needs per-time visibility.

Aetheria's fog is a grid-owned world volume sampled by a stochastic temporal camera raymarch. Shared 2D fields provide surface height, patch density/height, tint, and flow; the raymarch uses Halton plus blue-noise offsets, quadratic distance spacing, Beer-Lambert integration, temporal reprojection, and history clipping. Its signature horizon-scale motion comes from phase-paired scrolling triangle noise advected through global/slope flow, not from storing or raymarching a giant persistent 3D volume.

Aetheria's post fog cannot write depth, so transparent-looking VFX that must interact with fog/depth/shadows use stochastic cutout instead of ordinary alpha blending. `Aetheria/Dithered Particles` renders as AlphaTest/TransparentCutout, clips alpha against blue-noise plus a frame-varying golden-ratio offset, and applies matching coverage in its shadow caster pass so TAA can reconcile the stipple into perceived transparency.

The first Aquarium field-first renderer pass should live beside the existing gravity/stardust domain, not in a separate screen-space effect. Raymarch camera rays through SDF solids and gassy SDF density while sampling the shared gravity texture for surface height/tint, feeding agent and pointer sources into density, using phase-paired triangle noise for cheap flow, and preserving stochastic coverage for solid/transparent-depth participation.

Bruneton atmospheric scattering should steer Aquarium's global atmosphere as a precomputed transport cache: transmittance, scattering, optional single-Mie, and irradiance textures are generated by an explicit pass graph with per-order delta textures, then runtime shaders query them for sky radiance, aerial perspective, and surface irradiance. Local gassy SDF fog should remain dynamic/stochastic but be lit and composed against these cached global fields.

summary: Swarm bodies moved out of traditional Three geometry and into the field-volume shader. Invisible groups remain as projection anchors; visible bodies are chrome planet SDFs with local-domain cheap 4D fBm displacement, mass-scaled gaseous atmospheres, and solar Self shading/corona noise. The initial nested value-noise version built but was too expensive for smoke-scale headless rendering; compact analytic fBm kept the visual contract while restoring visual smoke.

Documented the current renderer as a hybrid Three/Aetheria gravity-domain plus fullscreen analytic SDF/gas raymarch. It is not currently a sparse brick map or Wronski froxel pipeline: the shader reconstructs a ray per pixel, marches analytic fields, samples the moving 2D gravity texture, and integrates Beer-Lambert gas directly. Future architecture should add typed SDF sources, optional sparse bricks only for non-cheap derived fields, froxel injection/integration, depth-aware composition, stochastic TAA, and Bruneton global atmosphere.

Moved the preferred agent/fog field renderer onto real WebGPU compute. The froxel compute pass writes one u32 primitive-membership bitmask per froxel into a storage buffer; the WebGPU render pass samples that mask while marching and evaluates only the agent planet/atmosphere primitives named by the current froxel. Avoid WebGPU-to-WebGL readback/upload; Three/WebGL remains the moving grid and fallback field path only.

Adjusted the WebGPU field march so solid SDF and volumetric atmosphere evaluation share the same froxel primitive bitmask. Each ray sample reads the current froxel's primitive membership, evaluates only those primitives, and terminates the march when a solid SDF is touched, shading the solid with accumulated fog/transmittance up to the hit.

Copied Aetheria's abstract studio HDR into the Aquarium public assets, loaded it through Three RGBELoader, filtered it through PMREM, and assigned it to scene.environment for PBR lighting. The WebGPU field chrome path cannot sample WebGL PMREM textures directly, so it currently uses a matching warm-key/cool-fill studio response until HDR parsing/prefiltering is owned by the WebGPU resource graph.

Added a WebGPU first-order spherical-harmonic lighting cache in froxel space. After primitive masks are built, a compute pass ping-pongs four RGB coefficients per froxel, blends previous lighting with six-neighbor propagation, injects a sampled summary of studio3.hdr from volume edges, and injects Self as a warm local emitter. The field march samples those coefficients for gas in-scattering and solid diffuse wrap, while the old screen-depth baseline haze was removed and planet displacement frequencies were lowered.

Corrected froxel fitting: keep x/y froxel dimensions canvas-local and screen-aligned, and fit only the near/far depth interval to the projected moving grid volume. Three projects the grid-volume depth bounds and passes them to WebGPU; agent primitive data now carries projected body depth, so primitive masks, SH propagation, and the field march sample the live grid volume instead of an arbitrary full-depth corridor.

Normalized agent solid body radius across the WebGPU froxel field and WebGL fallback SDF paths. WebGPU no longer derives body radius from z/expression/acknowledgement or a Self multiplier, and the fallback sourceRadius now returns a fixed solid radius. Removed the old DOM caption z-elevation offset so labels remain anchored to the Three-projected body position instead of bobbing independently, which was most visible on Self.

Corrected the WebGPU body radius from fixed screen pixels to projected world-space behavior. All planets still share one base world radius, but the pixel radius is multiplied by Three's projected camera scale so zooming in enlarges the SDF bodies and allows surface inspection without reintroducing state-driven or Self-specific size changes.

Reasserted that the fitted grid/fog volume is the visibility window. World-space solid planet hits and atmospheric density now apply a smooth near/far depth-window fade instead of allowing solids to render outside the current grid area of interest.

Removed the projection-scale body-size patch from the conceptual model. The WebGPU field renderer now receives Three's camera position plus frustum corner rays, reconstructs each pixel ray in world space, intersects shared-radius planet SDFs against world-space agent centers, and uses projected primitive data only for froxel/screen culling.

Separated swarm registration from liveness. If the selected Epiphany has no heartbeat/running role/job signals, the Aquarium renders registered members as sleeping cold white dwarf bodies instead of showing the EpiphanyAgent specialist constellation. The Tauri snapshot path now returns a sleeping standalone status if the harness status bridge is unreachable, so the Aquarium can still run by itself.

Promoted the WebGPU froxel/marching path to the visible aquarium stage. The old Three grid canvas is hidden, the WebGPU overlay is visible, and the field shader now renders a procedural PowerPulse heightfield grid surface plus a fog bank over it while continuing to shade SDF bodies and atmospheres from world-space camera rays.

Started the migration from the web-shaped Aquarium renderer to a Bevy-native Rust host. The new host lives in bevy-aquarium, uses Bevy 0.18 for world-space camera/body/spring/heightfield scaffolding, uses cultcache-rs for typed client settings and presence persistence, and uses cultnet-rs to construct its runtime hello and advertise supported document types. Future renderer work should land in this host rather than adding more ad hoc renderer machinery to React/Tauri.

Encoded the Bevy camera target as the Grid center invariant. CameraRig target is clamped to the global XY plane, GridFrame.center follows it, GridFrame.half_extent scales with camera distance, pointer/cursor gravity is clipped to the moving square, and the heightfield mesh is rebuilt over the same domain that future gravity render targets should use as their heightmap footprint.
